recipes.name: Grandma's Creamy Potato Salad with Sour Cream
ingredients_raw: 2 dill pickle spears, chopped, or more to taste

steps.text: Place potatoes in a large pot and cover with salted water; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until tender, 20 to 30 minutes. Drain and cool slightly. Slice potatoes into a large bowl.

Combine mayonnaise, sour cream, yogurt, onions, pickles, mustard, horseradish, celery seed, salt, pepper, garlic, onion salt, and garlic powder in a small bowl; mix until combined. Pour dressing over sliced potatoes and toss to coat. Gently stir in eggs.
Cover and refrigerate for 2 to 3 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma's Creamy Potato Salad with Sour Cream
raw_recipe.description: This amazing potato salad takes some time to make but is so worth it. It gets its creaminess from sour cream, mayonnaise, and yogurt.

review.reviewBody: Whew, there are a lot of ingredients for potato salad. I didn’t have onion salt, so sub’d onion powder, and I’m not convinced that you need both minced garlic and garlic powder. The dressing does taste pretty good with a nice tang from the horseradish. I mixed up the dressing as written, but there was just too much of it for the amount of potatoes which I’d weighed, and I didn’t use all of the dressing. I make tasty potato salad with mayo and Greek yogurt with perfect consistency, and I have to wonder if sour cream is even necessary. Although it does thicken a little when the potato salad is chilled, it’s still too much on the wet side. This could be a personal preference, but if I were to make again, I’d chunk the potatoes instead of slicing them, since they pretty much fell apart, even when gently combining ingredients. We eat a lot of different potato salads, and unfortunately, it’s doubtful I’ll make this one again, but thanks for sharing your Grandma’s recipe.
